lm_output:
The passage describes a group of people who are virtuous and upright. They do not turn to evil, but instead turn to the good. They do not use oaths, as they neither distrust nor deceive anyone. They do not desire money or empty glory, as their treasure is in heaven and they refer all things to the glory of Christ.

The passage also criticizes someone named Luther, stating that he is inconsistent in his beliefs, as he says one thing at the beginning of an assertion and something else later on, recanting what he said before. The passage suggests that Luther is put off by this inconsistency.
